overview: One is a leading cause of serious infection worldwide; the other is usually harmless skin flora that only matters when it shouldn't be there.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A coagulase-positive staphylococcus and a major human pathogen capable of a wide range of infections.
aspects.valueB: A coagulase-negative staphylococcus that is part of normal skin flora but can act as an opportunist.

aspects.label: Key Virulence Factors
aspects.valueA: Protein A, coagulase, toxins (TSST-1, PVL, enterotoxins), biofilm.
aspects.valueB: Biofilm formation via polysaccharide intercellular adhesin is its main virulence mechanism.

aspects.label: Clinical Significance
aspects.valueA: True pathogen — causes skin/soft tissue infections, bacteremia, endocarditis, osteomyelitis.
aspects.valueB: Common contaminant in blood cultures; true pathogen mainly in the setting of indwelling devices (catheters, prosthetics).

aspects.label: Interpretation When Isolated From Blood
aspects.valueA: A single positive blood culture is usually treated as clinically significant.
aspects.valueB: Often dismissed as contamination unless isolated from multiple cultures or a patient with a device.

aspects.label: Antibiotic Resistance Concern
aspects.valueA: MRSA (methicillin-resistant strains) is a major public health concern.
aspects.valueB: Frequently multidrug-resistant given its device-associated niche, though less publicized than MRSA.

overlay.commonMisconception: A coagulase-negative Staph in blood culture isn't automatically 'nothing' — context (device, repeat cultures) decides.
